name: Längenfeld
kurzbeschreibung: Home of the Aqua Dome and starting point for hikes into the inner Ötztal. Famous for its thermal springs.
beschreibung:
Overview

Längenfeld is an expansive alpine municipality situated in the heart of the Ötztal valley in the Tyrolean Oberland. Occupying a wide, sunlit valley basin at an altitude of 1,179 metres along the Ötztaler Ache river, the community is framed by towering three-thousand-metre summits of the Stubai and Ötztal Alps. Home to approximately 4,900 residents, Längenfeld is the most populous municipality in the valley and serves as a premier hub for wellness, outdoor recreation, and mountaineering. The town is renowned across Europe for the futuristic Aqua Dome thermal spa complex, utilizing natural thermal sulfur springs, and for its tranquil tributary hamlet of Gries in the Sulztal.

History

The fertile valley plain of Längenfeld has been cultivated since early medieval times, first documented in 1288 in a ducal land register under the name Lenginvelt. For generations, local livelihoods relied upon arduous high-altitude farming and flax production. The restorative thermal sulfur springs of historic Bad Längenfeld attracted health seekers as early as the 16th century, though the original spring ceased flowing in the 1970s. In 1997, deep subterranean drilling successfully tapped into geothermal sulfur water at a depth of 1,865 metres. This breakthrough made possible the construction of the Aqua Dome resort, opened in 2004, transforming Längenfeld into an internationally celebrated year-round wellness destination.

Getting There

Längenfeld is conveniently accessible via major transit routes. Motorists depart the A12 Inntal Autobahn at the Haiming-Ötztal exit and follow the well-engineered B186 Ötztal federal road southward for approximately 25 kilometres directly into the village. Rail travelers arrive at Ötztal-Bahnhof along the Arlberg Railway line. From the station forecourt, frequent regional buses operated by Ötztaler Verkehrsgesellschaft run on a 30-minute schedule throughout the valley, stopping at multiple conveniently located stations within Längenfeld.

Tips

A rejuvenating visit to the Aqua Dome – Tirol Therme Längenfeld is essential, where futuristic floating outdoor basin pools provide mineral-rich warm soaks framed by majestic glacier views. Experienced climbers will appreciate the thrilling granite via ferratas at the Lehner Waterfall and the Reinhard-Schiestl route on the Burgstein cliffs. Hikers with a head for heights should traverse the 84-metre Burgstein suspension bridge swinging over the gorge. Cultural heritage comes alive at the Ötztal Open-Air Museum in Lehn, while the tranquil mountain village of Gries offers access to alpine hikes towards the Amberger Hütte.
